tweets.text:
i started bidding and buying here.

not because things have changed. actually, not much has. but something important did.

we're still following equities. the Fed is still ahead of us, macro is a mess, and there's enough geopolitical risk out there to send bitcoin down $5k in a single candle.

i still think we could see $75k, maybe even lower if someone big capitulates and takes everyone down with them.

but here's what's interesting.

the same people who were calling for $100k are now shorting $80k. every influencer suddenly has a very convincing explanation for why we need to go lower.
and after all the shit we've been through, bitcoin is still around $80k.

that's worth paying attention to.

one positive headline or stocks ticking up and we're back at $83k, $85k. maybe even $90k before the next bad headline hits.

imagine everyone waiting for the big capitulation candle, and when it finally comes, bitcoin dumps from $90k to $85k instead of $80k to $75k.

the level everyone was terrified of becomes support.

and the same people shorting $80k will be explaining why $100k was inevitable.

i'm not calling the bottom. but I started buying again.

tweets.text:
I think we’re entering an interesting phase for AI trading, where trust is becoming just as important as performance.

Hacken’s research shows that 84.8% of surveyed crypto traders have already used AI for research or trading.

But there’s still a clear line when it comes to giving AI control, only 6.5% would let it manage more than half of their account.

What caught my attention is that @MEXC found willingness to automate increases from 55% to 71.8% when proper risk limits are in place.

And 95.5% want at least one mandatory safeguard.

For me, that says a lot: people aren’t against AI taking control. They just want to know there are guardrails.

The future of AI trading may be less about full autonomy and more about controlled autonomy. Do you agree?

tweets.text:
Maybe it seems as if there was little technologic improvement in the crypto space over the past few years.

But one positive change is the revenue crypto companies are generating. This has been on a steady climb over the years. Never hitting below $1B+ a month since late 2024.

One thing to note, about 70% of this is Tether and Circle. With the rising interest rates and ever growing stablecoin supply this has obviously been the biggest driver.

But even if you take those two out, there is considerable improvement over the years even by the Crypto native projects that are solely operating within the sector. $HYPE is the obvious big example.

This trend has in turn caused for improved tokenomics in a lot of those projects. Focussing more on revenue and buybacks to award token holders and make them benefit to a larger degree.

Good change overall obviously. Now the biggest thing is the amount of projects and large investor unlocks that are still a big pain for the market.

tweets.text:
Did you know over $20,000,000,000,000 is benchmarked to S&P stock indices?

And now the company behind the S&P 500 is launching prediction market indices with Kalshi.

Crazy that we went from "wtf is kalshi?" to the world's largest index company turning prediction markets into an institutional asset class.

quote.text:
S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

Think about what that opens up.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

tweets.text:
What's most likely to crash markets in 2027?

I spent the morning looking at exactly that. Not predictions, just probabilities.

The biggest risks for the next 12 to 18 months in my opinion are:

• A sharp selloff in AI stocks
• A major AI-driven cyberattack
• The Federal Reserve making a policy mistake
• The war with Iran escalating
• Turmoil in the bond market

Other big ones on the list:

• Rising US-China tensions
• A messy fight over the US debt limit
• An escalating global trade war
• Job losses driven by AI
• Another global pandemic
• A slump in commercial real estate

A crypto crash ranks as likely, but low on damage to the wider economy.

For $BTC, that macro mix matters more than any crypto headline. 

If AI stocks unwind and the Fed gets it wrong, liquidity dries up everywhere.

Which one worries you most, and what's missing from this list? Let me know below 👇

tweets.text:
$BTC Another day sitting at the $80K support.

Neither bull or bear seems to be able to get this market moving in any direction at this point.

I do stand by my point of yesterday. Even in a non ideal outcome of all the upcoming events, once they are done with, the market has certainty which helps the bulls more than the bears.

So if the bears want to see lower levels, it should happen sooner than later for that scenario to play out in my opinion.

The more selling gets absorbed down here during all this uncertainty without a breakdown, the more likely it is that we'll see seller exhaustion at some point and the market just starts grinding higher.

quote.text:
$BTC Big week(s).

Either Bitcoin holds $80K throughout these next 1-2 weeks with: FOMC, Earnings, Election(s), IPO filing(s), End/Start of the month flows & whatever geopolitical headlines we're going to see.

In that case I think we go to $87K and take out those equal highs there and target $90K+.

If price does lose $80K we'll find ourselves in a solid high timeframe value area (I think) in the mid to low $70Ks. Might chop around there for a while and things will look scary. But from there I do believe we have a good chance of setting that higher timeframe higher low from the big impulse from $58K to the recent high at $87K.

Best to keep an eye on the headlines and see how the market reacts. That will be leading.

I think sentiment and outlook is pretty bearish already so if we were to absorb whatever selling happens down here and prices just start grinding up that'd be a big sign of strength to me and at that case I think this will just keep drifting up by shorts covering and sidelined/derisked capital moving back in over the days.

It's going to be very easy to get chopped up or shaken out of your bias in the next 1-2 weeks I think.

Easiest to just play things level by level and go from there. Don't assume supports or resistances break until you actually see it broken (on a daily candle close for example). That is how many people keep getting caught off guard.
